name: Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares
summary:
Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares, was a Spanish royal favourite of Philip IV and minister from 1621 to 1643. He was appointed as Grandee on April 10, 1621, and played a key role in shaping state policy in Spain until January 1643.

During his rule, he over-exerted Spain in foreign affairs and unsuccessfully attempted domestic reform. His policy of committing Spain to recapture Holland led to economic strain and diplomatic tensions with other European powers. Despite these challenges, Olivares remained a dominant figure in Spanish politics until his death on July 22, 1645.

Olivares' legacy is complex and multifaceted. He is remembered for his efforts to modernize Spain's institutions and promote its interests abroad, but also for his authoritarianism and inability to address the country's deep-seated social and economic problems.

The Count-Duke of Olivares died on July 22, 1645, at the age of 69. His death marked the end of an era in Spanish history, as the country began to transition towards a new period of relative stability and prosperity.

In conclusion, the Count-Duke of Olivares was a pivotal figure in Spanish history, whose policies and actions had far-reaching consequences for the country and its people.
